'''Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri''' (born 1 March 1952) is an Indian [[Condensed matter physics|condensed matter]] physicist, materials scientist and a Distinguished Emeritus Professor at the [[S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]]. Known for his pioneering work on the interplay of disorder and interaction, Raychaudhuri is an elected fellow of all the three major Indian science academies viz. [[Indian Academy of Sciences]], [[National Academy of Sciences, India]] and [[Indian National Science Academy]] as well as the Asia-Pacific Academy of Materials. He is a recipient of a number of awards such as Millennium Medal of the [[Indian Science Congress]], ICS Gold Medal of the Materials Research Society of India and FICCI Award. The [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], the apex agency of the Government of India for scientific research, awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology]], one of the highest Indian science awards, for his contributions to physical sciences in 1994.<ref name="View Bhatnagar Awardees">{{cite web | url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/AwardeeList.aspx | title=View Bhatnagar Awardees | publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize | date=2016 | access-date=12 November 2016}}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Long link - please select award year to see details}}

== Biography ==
[[File:S N Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences, Main Building.jpg|thumb|left|S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]]
Born on 1 March 1952 in the Indian state of [[West Bengal]], Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri completed his BSc from [[Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda]] in 1973 and MSc from the [[Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur]] in 1975 before proceeding to [[Cornell University]] from where he secured a PhD in 1980, working under the supervision of Robert O. Pohl.<ref name="Profile on IISc">{{Cite web |url=http://www.physics.iisc.ernet.in/~arup/cv.pdf |title=Profile on IISc |date=2017-10-16 |website=Indian Institute of Science |access-date=2017-10-16}}</ref> His post-doctoral studies were at [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]] as an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt fellow]] and on his return to India in 1982, he joined the [[Indian Institute of Science]] as a lecturer.{{citation needed|date=November 2017}} He continued at IISc until 1997 during which period, he served as an assistant professor and as an associate professor before becoming a professor in 1997. The same year, he moved to the [[National Physical Laboratory of India]] as its director on deputation for a three-year stint and returned to IISc in 2000 to resume his duties as a professor. At IISC, he also chaired the Central Cryogenic Facility from 1993 to 1997 and served as the convener of the ''Integrated PhD Programme'' from 1994 to 1997. In 2004, he returned to his home state to join [[S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences]] as a senior professor and served as its director from 2006 until his superannuation from service.<ref name="Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri  - Professor & Director ">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/fac_new/arupkumarraychaudhuri.html.201304100915 |title=Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri - Professor & Director |date=2017-10-16 |website=S. N. Bose National Centre for Basic Sciences |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180131231044/http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/fac_new/arupkumarraychaudhuri.html.201304100915 |archive-date=31 January 2018 }}</ref> Post retirement, he continues his association with S. N. Bose National Centre by holding the positions of a Distinguished Emeritus Professor<ref name="Director & Distinguished Professor">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/arup.htm |title=Director & Distinguished Professor |date=2017-10-16 |website=S. N. Bose National Centre |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016225925/http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/arup.htm |archive-date=16 October 2017 }}</ref> and the Nodal Officer of its Technical Research Center project.<ref name="Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri-Distinguished Professor (Emeritus)">{{Cite web |url=http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/fac_new/arupkumarraychaudhuri.html |title=Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri-Distinguished Professor (Emeritus) |date=2017-10-16 |website=S. N. Bose National Centre |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016225922/http://www.bose.res.in/faculty/fac_new/arupkumarraychaudhuri.html |archive-date=16 October 2017 }}</ref>

== Legacy ==
[[File:Perovskite-155026.jpg|thumb|235px|Perovskite crystals]]
Raychaudhuri's work have mainly been in the disciplines of material science and condensed matter physics, particularly on the physics of transition metal oxides such as [[perovskite]] oxides.<ref name="Indian fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P01-1301 |title=Indian fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=2 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190202205235/http://insaindia.res.in/detail/P01-1301 }}</ref> Glassy state and High Tc superconductor physics and colossal magnetoresistance have been some of his other interests and his research has helped in the elucidation of the interplay of disorder and interaction.<ref name="Brief Profile of the Awardee">{{Cite web |url=http://ssbprize.gov.in/Content/Detail.aspx?AID=464 |title=Brief Profile of the Awardee |date=2017 |publisher=Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize |access-date=2017-08-23}}</ref> Towards the later part of his career, he worked on ''nanofabrications using nanolithography techniques''. He is also credited with the development of an indigenous low temperature scanning tunneling microscope and a host of other experiment equipment.<ref name="Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners">{{cite web | url=http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | title=Handbook of Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize Winners | publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research | date=1999 | access-date=16 October 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304043957/http://www.csirhrdg.res.in/ssb.pdf | archive-date=4 March 2016 }}</ref> His studies have been documented by way of a number of articles<ref name="On Google Scholar">{{Cite web |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=n0lJv9oAAAAJ&hl=en |title=On Google Scholar |date=2017 |publisher=Google Scholar}}</ref><ref name="On ResearchGate">{{Cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Arup_Raychaudhuri |title=On ResearchGate |date=2017 }}</ref>{{Refn|group=note|Please see ''Selected bibliography'' section}} and the online article repository of the Indian Academy of Sciences has listed 172 of them.<ref name="Browse by Fellow">{{Cite web |url=http://repository.ias.ac.in/view/fellows/Raychaudhuri=3AArup_Kumar=3A=3A.html |title=Browse by Fellow |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

Raychaudhuri is known to have contributed to the development of integrated doctoral programs at IISc as the head of the program during 1994–97.<ref name="Indian fellow" /> He has served as a member of the ''Commission on Low Temperature Physics'' of the [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] and 35 doctoral researchers have been mentored by him.<ref name="Arup Kumar Raychaudhuri-Distinguished Professor (Emeritus)" />

== Awards and honors ==
In 1986, The Indian Physics Association awarded the N. S. Sathyamurthy Award for young scientists to Raychaudhuri.<ref name="N.S. Satyamurthy Award">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ipa1970.org.in/nslist.php |title=N.S. Satyamurthy Award |date=2017-10-16 |website=Indian Physics Association |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016225826/http://www.ipa1970.org.in/nslist.php |archive-date=16 October 2017 }}</ref> The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research awarded him the [[Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize]], one of the highest Indian science awards in 1994.<ref name="CSIR list of Awardees">{{Cite web |url=http://www.csir.res.in/careeraward/prize-winner-indexdiscipline-wise |title=CSIR list of Awardees |date=2017 |publisher=Council of Scientific and Industrial Research}}</ref> He received the MRSI Medal of the Materials Research Society of India in 1996; the society would honour him again in 2002 with the MRSI-ICSC Super Conductivity and Materials Science Annual Prize.<ref name="MRSI Awards and Honours">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mrsi.org.in/awardshonours.php |title=MRSI Awards and Honours |date=2017-10-16 |website=Materials Research Society of India |access-date=2017-10-16}}</ref> The [[Indian Science Congress]] selected him for the Millennium Medal in 2000 and three years later, he received the 2003 FICCI Award in materials science and applied sciences. The [[Indian National Science Academy]] honored him with the Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal in 2008.<ref name="Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal ">{{Cite web |url=http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 |title=Homi Jehangir Bhabha Medal |date=2017-10-16 |website=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-date=16 September 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916233840/http://insaindia.res.in/recipients.php#34 }}</ref>

Raychaudhuri has held several research fellowships which include the [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt fellowship]] (1980) as well as the J. C. Bose National fellowship of the [[Department of Science and Technology (India)|Department of Science and Technology]] (2006) and was an Associate of the [[Indian Academy of Sciences]] (1986), Nuclear Science Centre (1996) and  [[National Institute of Advanced Studies]] (1996).<ref name="Profile on IISc" /> The Indian Academy of Sciences elected him as a fellow in 1993, the same year as he received the honorary senior fellowship of the [[Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research]].<ref name="Fellow profile">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ias.ac.in/describe/fellow/Raychaudhuri,_Prof._Arup_Kumar |title=Fellow profile |date=2017 |publisher=Indian Academy of Sciences}}</ref> The year 2000 brought him two elected fellowships, those of [[National Academy of Sciences, India]]<ref name="NASI fellows">{{Cite web |url=http://www.nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=R |title=NASI fellows |date=2017 |publisher=National Academy of Sciences, India |access-date=16 October 2017 |archive-date=15 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160315130140/http://nasi.org.in/fellows.asp?RsFilter=R }}</ref> and Asia-Pacific Academy of Materials which was followed by the elected fellowship of Indian National Science Academy a year later.<ref name="INSA Year Book 2016">{{Cite web |url=http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |title=INSA Year Book 2016 |date=2017-10-16 |publisher=Indian National Science Academy |access-date=2017-10-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161104001952/http://www.insaindia.res.in/pdf/YearBook_2016.pdf |archive-date=4 November 2016 }}</ref> He was also selected for the honorary professorship by the Jawaharlal Nehru Centre for Advanced Scientific Research in 2000. The award orations delivered by him include Platinum Jubilee Lecture of [[Indian Science Congress]] in 1999.<ref name="Profile on IISc" />
